title: Granular runtime energy accounting and telemetry playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This playbook documents the instrumentation, measurement methodology, and operational runbook for per-request and per-kernel energy accounting in the Redwood serving runtime. The goal is to provide a reproducible, low-noise measurement pipeline that ties energy consumption to SLOs, cost models, and regression gates used by runtime, infra, and perf teams.

Audience:
- Runtime engineers implementing kernel-level telemetry
- SRE and capacity teams performing capacity/cost forecasting
- Applied ML teams validating cost/quality tradeoffs for model variants

Goals and constraints:
- Provide request-level energy attribution within a bounded noise envelope (target: ±5% for steady-state long-running batches).
- Correlate per-token and per-request energy with kernel dispatch, kernel duration, and occupancy metrics.
- Avoid changes that materially affect scheduling behavior; default instrumentation must be low-overhead (<2% wall-clock overhead on p95 latency for typical workloads).
- Produce artifacts that feed into the benchmarking suite and release regression gates.

When to use:
- Baseline benchmarking for new kernel variants or quantized model builds.
- Cost regression detection during release and canary phases.
- Capacity planning when optimizing for energy-constrained regions or on-prem runtimes.

Telemetry model (schema):
Each emitted energy record is a single-line JSON event (or protobuf) with the following fields. The runtime telemetry collector should batch and compress these events for downstream storage.

| field | type | description | example |
|-------|------|-------------|---------|
| timestamp_utc | string | RFC3339 timestamp at sample emission | 2025-02-08T16:42:10.123Z |
| node_id | string | unique node identifier (hw+pool) | gpu-ec2-p4d-12-3 |
| gpu_index | integer | local GPU ordinal on the node | 0 |
| sample_type | string | one of: kernel_start, kernel_end, power_sample | kernel_start |
| sample_id | string | correlation id to join start/end/power samples | samp-abc-123 |
| request_id | string | optional request id when available | req-3d9f |
| model_variant | string | model id + quantization suffix | llama2-13b-q4 |
| kernel_name | string | runtime kernel or op name | attention_fused |
| wall_time_ms | number | duration in ms for kernel_start/kernel_end events | 2.6 |
| power_watts | number | instantaneous power measurement for power_sample | 210.5 |
| energy_joules | number | derived energy for the interval (if provided) | 0.55 |
| batch_size | integer | number of sequences/tokens in kernel invocation | 8 |
| seq_len | integer | sequence length payload for this kernel | 96 |
| tags | list[string] | additional labels (can include canary/cohort) | ["canary","gpu-fe"] |

Note: If the GPU vendor API yields only power samples, the ingestion pipeline must correlate power samples with kernel_start/kernel_end via sample_id and compute energy_joules = integrate(power_watts over time). The runtime should prefer hardware power sensors; fall back to model-based estimators when sensors are unavailable.

Measurement procedure (step-by-step):
1. Testbed setup
   - Use a dedicated cluster to avoid background noise (isolated queue, pinned GPUs, no other tenants).
   - Ensure node thermal state is stable: run a 15-minute warmup workload at target concurrency before measurement.
   - Disable DVFS or other dynamic power policies where possible; record firmware/driver versions.
2. Instrumentation
   - Enable kernel_start/kernel_end hooks around the kernel dispatch layer. Hooks must be high-resolution (microsecond clock).
   - Sample GPU power at 100Hz (or max supported) from hw telemetry; annotate with GPU clock/pstate where available.
   - Tag every request with a lightweight correlation id propagated from HTTP ingress to scheduler to kernel dispatch.
3. Data collection
   - Collect a minimum of N=1,000 similar request samples per model variant and shape to achieve stable aggregates.
   - Record the same workload under three concurrency shapes: low (single request), medium (SLO-target concurrency), and high (2x SLO concurrency) to capture contention effects.
4. Post-processing
   - Join kernel_start/kernel_end with power samples by sample_id and compute per-kernel energy in joules.
   - Aggregate per-request energy by summing kernel energies for all kernels attributed to a request_id.
   - Compute per-token energy by dividing per-request energy by generated tokens (or input+output tokens for inference accounting).

Benchmark protocol and acceptance criteria:
- Benchmark runs must be reproducible and declared in a manifest: workload description (prompt distribution), model commit, kernel build id, driver version, node topology, and network baseline.
- Reported metrics: median and p95 per-request energy (J), per-token energy (mJ/token), p95 latency, and delta from baseline (percentage).
- Acceptance gate for release: no >10% increase in median per-token energy without a commensurate latency or quality improvement. For targeted low-power builds, require p95 latency <= SLO and per-token energy reduction >= 15%.

Noise characterization and correction:
- Use paired experiments when comparing two variants on the same warmed cluster to reduce environmental variance.
- Apply a rolling median filter to power sample streams to remove transient spikes (e.g., fan spin-up).
- If ambient temperature shifts >3°C during a long run, invalidate the run and re-measure.

Operational runbook: energy-related SLO breach
1. Detection
   - Alert triggers: sustained >15% increase in per-token energy vs baseline on production traffic for 3 consecutive hours, or abnormal GPU power profile (fan at max, repeated thermal throttling events).
2. Triage steps
   - Identify affected nodes via node_id and cross-check driver/firmware changes in the last rollout.
   - Check kernel_build and model_variant tags for recent rollouts (use release manifest).
   - Run the short diagnostic job (see commands below) on a suspect node to confirm instrumentation readings.
3. Immediate mitigations
   - If a specific kernel variant is implicated, route traffic to previous kernel build using the runtime's rollout API (canary->stable rollback).
   - If thermal/firmware issue: cordon node, shift traffic, and notify infra to schedule remediation.
4. Postmortem and prevention
   - Add the failing trace and energy profile to the fidelity regression harness.
   - If root cause is scheduler-induced contention, update the scheduler hinting table to add a slot reservation for that workload shape.

Example diagnostic commands:
- Collect a 60s power trace on node: 
  sudo /opt/redwood/bin/gpu_power_capture --duration 60 --sample-rate 100 --out /tmp/power-$(date +%s).ndjson
- Run a local microbenchmark that replays the production sequence shapes: 
  /opt/redwood/bin/runtime_bench --model llama2-13b-q4 --shape-file shapes.yaml --iterations 200 --emit-energy --tag debug-2025

YAML manifest snippet (benchmark-declaration):

workload: "chat-short-prompts"
model: "llama2-13b-q4"
kernel_build: "kbuild-2025-03-12-rc3"
driver: "nvidia-560.12"
node_topology: "p4d-24x-gpu"
shapes: ["single-1","slo-8","burst-32"]
notes: "warmup 15m; ambient target 22C +/- 2C"

Appendix A — Example aggregation queries (pseudo-SQL):
- Per-token energy median: 
  SELECT model_variant, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (energy_joules / tokens) AS median_mj_per_token
  FROM energy_events JOIN request_tokens USING(request_id)
  WHERE sample_time BETWEEN :start AND :end AND cohort='prod'
  GROUP BY model_variant;
- Kernel-level energy hotlist: 
  SELECT kernel_name, SUM(energy_joules) AS total_joules, COUNT(DISTINCT request_id) AS requests
  FROM kernel_energy_samples
  WHERE sample_time BETWEEN :start AND :end
  GROUP BY kernel_name
  ORDER BY total_joules DESC
  LIMIT 50;

Appendix B — Implementation notes for runtime engineers:
- Keep kernel_start/kernel_end as a minimal shim that only emits a correlation id and timestamp. Heavy processing must be deferred to the telemetry collector to avoid scheduler perturbation.
- Use asynchronous, lock-free buffers for power sample ingestion to avoid blocking kernel dispatch threads.
- When hardware sensors are not accessible (e.g., some on-prem vendors), implement a calibrated estimator that maps kernel duration and occupancy to energy. Calibration must be performed against hardware-sensor baseline across multiple shapes.

Appendix C — Known limitations and future work:
- Attribution across multi-GPU kernels (model parallel) increases complexity; current approach attributes energy to the initiating GPU and annotates cross-GPU spans for approximate redistribution. A planned follow-up (Q2 2025) will add cross-GPU energy stitching.
- NVLink and interconnect power contributions are currently excluded; roadmap includes capturing node-level PSU metrics in a future iteration.
